sections.h2: Paying a Warren County tax bill
sections.html:
The tax office is at 117 S. Main St. in Warrenton, 27589, beside the courthouse. Mail goes to PO Box 240, Warrenton, NC 27589. The office observes most national holidays.

Some payment routes carry fees, so it helps to know the free ones.

  • Phone 1-866-483-9680 or use warren.webtaxpay.com. Charges are $3.95 for a debit card, 2.60 percent of the amount for a credit card, and $2.50 for a check or eCheck.
  • A mailed check costs nothing.
  • The drop box to the right of the office door is also free.

The tax administrator answers to the commissioners and the county manager, and also to the state Department of Revenue and Property Tax Commission.

The county rate on real and personal property for 2026-2027 is $0.5950 per $100. Confirm it with the tax office before you rely on it for a sale.

Warren last revalued in 2025. Those assessments stay in place until 2032 unless an owner adds something such as a garage, a room or a new house, and the next revaluation is slated for 2033. A private appraisal company assists the county.

The long gap affects a sale. A buyer's tax value stays on the 2025 appraisal, whatever the contract price, until the building changes.

The 2026 bills are due September 1 but not delinquent until January 6, 2027, so January 5 is the last clean day. Then 2 percent applies for January, plus three-fourths of one percent for each later month.

The county's yearly calendar shows what follows if you fall behind.

Warren County yearly tax steps
WhenWhat happens
January 1Ownership and value fixed; real property appeals open
January 6Interest starts; enforced collection, up to foreclosure, follows
January 31Listing period ends; 10 percent late penalty
March and AprilLetters in March; unpaid accounts advertised in April
June 1Relief applications due
AugustAnnual tax bills mailed
September 1Current year taxes due

sections.h2: Recording a deed with taxes owed
sections.html:
You need either a tax certification or an attorney's statement. Since January 7, 2026, a commissioners' resolution under G.S. 161-31 bars the Register of Deeds from accepting a transfer deed unless the Tax Collector certifies that no delinquent taxes are a lien.

The alternative is a statement added by the closing attorney that delinquent taxes will be paid at closing. Bring the deed to the Tax Collector between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. so staff can research the parcel and stamp it if warranted.

Check the tax account well before closing. Several unpaid years do not block a sale, but the arrears come out of your proceeds and the office needs research time.

sections.h2: How a Warren County value appeal works
sections.html:
Each January 1 opens the real property appeal window, which closes when the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns. An informal appeal form is posted under Forms on the county site.

State law puts the board's first meeting between the first Mondays of April and May. Ask for your hearing before adjournment. A losing owner has 30 days from the mailed decision to notify the Property Tax Commission.

Two more points apply here. The owner bears the burden of showing a substantial overstatement, and market-value arguments are allowed only in a revaluation year. Vehicles, boats, trailers, aircraft and business equipment follow a different clock: 30 days from receiving the bill.

The path has three steps: informal appeal, formal appeal and the state Property Tax Commission. File a separate informal appeal form for each parcel, give your own opinion of value, and attach support for it.

  • Recent sales offered as support must have closed before the 1/1/2025 effective date of the revaluation. Later sales do not count.
  • Appraisals, photos of deferred maintenance and contractor estimates can go with the form.
  • Attorneys and tax representatives must supply a Power of Attorney.
  • Arguments based on the percentage increase from the last appraisal, the tax bill's size, economic conditions or the owner's ability to pay are not grounds for appeal.

If the informal review does not satisfy you, the formal appeal goes to the Board of Equalization and Review, a quasi-judicial setting where taxpayers give sworn testimony. A formal appeal filed after the board adjourns is heard the following tax year. From there, the Property Tax Commission requires Form AV-14, received or postmarked within 30 days of the board's mailed decision, and non-attorney representatives file Form AV-63.

The prior revaluation was effective 1/1/2017, so the 2025 change reflected eight years of market movement in one step.

Personal and business personal property is listed each January 1 to 31, with a 10 percent penalty for lateness. That list includes single wide mobile homes, farm equipment, unregistered vehicles, boats, aircraft, billboards and short-term rentals.

Land and buildings remain on the list for good, so nothing needs refiling each year unless the property changed. Request extensions by January 31. Mailed listings need a postmark by then, or April 15 with an extension. Get a mailing receipt.

Present use value matters to owners of working land. The minimums are:

  • Agricultural land: at least ten acres in commercial production of crops or animals.
  • Forest land: at least twenty acres meeting the forest requirements.
  • Horticultural land: at least five acres in commercial production of fruits, vegetables, nursery or floral products.
  • Agricultural and horticultural income: an average gross of $1,000 per year over three years; forest land has no income test.

Applications are due January 31. A buyer must apply within sixty days of a transfer, so mention enrollment to the buyer's attorney.

sections.h2: If a Warren County owner falls behind
sections.html:
Collection steps begin after January 6. Delinquent tax letters are mailed in March, and accounts still unpaid at the end of that month are advertised in the local paper in April. The tax office says enforced collection, up to and including foreclosure, can follow.

The tax lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date, with penalties, interest and costs added, and the county can bring a foreclosure action in the county where the property lies. A sale goes to the highest bidder at the courthouse door, where the commissioner may ask for a deposit of up to 20 percent of the bid. Exceptions or an increased bid may be filed within 10 days after the report of sale. A person redeeming before confirmation pays all taxes plus penalties, interest and costs.

Selling before any of this starts sidesteps the whole sequence. Phone the Warrenton tax office for your balance, then have your closing attorney pay it at the table. A cash sale moves quickly, so ask for the balance before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: Relief for older, disabled and veteran owners
sections.html:
File by June 1. A senior aged 65 or older can pick up an application beginning January 2. Owners claiming disability, or disabled veteran status, attach the A-9A or NCDVA-9 form as well.

The state's terms: $25,000 or half of appraised value, whichever is greater, for the elderly or disabled, with a $38,800 income limit for 2026; and $45,000 off for a disabled veteran with no age or income test. Only one of the three programs may be used. Present use value can save up to 90 percent.

If you inherited a Warren County house, ask the tax office whether a new application is needed.

faqs.q: When does Warren County tax interest begin?
faqs.a: January 6, 2027 for the 2026 bills. January 5 is the last interest-free day.

faqs.q: Does Warren County check taxes before recording a deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Either the Tax Collector certifies the taxes or the closing attorney adds a statement that delinquent taxes will be paid at closing. The rule took effect January 7, 2026.

faqs.q: How can I pay Warren County tax free of fees?
faqs.a: By mailed check or the drop box at 117 S. Main St. Card and eCheck payments carry fees.

faqs.q: When is Warren County's next revaluation?
faqs.a: The last one was in 2025, and the next is slated for 2033.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Warren County value?
faqs.a: Each January 1 opens the window for real property, and it closes when the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns. Start with the informal appeal form.
